dataset.name: CRMArena-Pro B2B Salesforce org (Salesforce AI Research)

notes: SCOPE. The snapshot was imported in full (no --until), before PR #26 (until-cutoff ingest) merged, so it covers the full timeline. Valid for WP6 extraction metrics only; this database must not be used for any HAR-129 decision run.

PROVENANCE. The database of the paid run was lost (the local embedded Postgres re-initialises its data directory on restart). This bundle is regenerated OFFLINE: a fresh local import of the same snapshot, then the 5144 recorded cassettes replayed through bench/data/crmarena_replay_worker.py (no network, no key): 5103 exact hits and 41 approximate hits (same email, known-people block ordered or classified differently by the new import). Latency, token, cost and provider-health numbers still come from the original worker and core logs of the paid run.

ENVIRONMENT. Local embedded Postgres 17 (Windows, WIN1252-labelled; read as UTF-8 by the tools). Paid run: worker in record mode, deepseek-v4-flash via OpenRouter (answering model deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash), prompt/extractor extract-v4, 24 core coalescers, 24 concurrent worker calls. No Neon or shared database.

PILOT. 5% stratified by activity type (seed 20261002): 261 emails (EmailSent 147, EmailReceived 92, EmailReply 22) of 5177, the rest held out with empty cached answers; 260 answered. Reported cost 0.108 USD, 0.000391 USD per event, 2.02 USD projected for all 5177, far below the 10 USD cap, so the full run went ahead.

COST. Attributable cost = what OpenRouter reported in our own successful responses plus every abandoned (hung) attempt priced as a mean call (see the cost line). The shared key's meter moved 23.87 USD in the same hours, but it is not our spend: it moved 0.19 USD in one minute while all our cores were stopped, and the key later returned HTTP 402 (see COVERAGE).

COVERAGE AND PROVIDER ERRORS. From 05:27Z the provider answered the worker with HTTP 402 (payment required: the shared key ran out of credit) on and off; the worker turned each into a 502 provider_error. 32,424 such failed calls followed, because parked recompute jobs retry every 10 minutes with no circuit breaker on a persistent provider error. The 41 emails of the paid run that were never extracted (33 in this replay: 5144 of 5177 extracted) therefore failed on the provider side, not on their content; their 7 accounts' jobs parked after 5 attempts. The earlier summary 'model provider failed to produce a usable result' was the worker's public message for these 402s.

PARKING LOSES THE STATE. A job whose model call fails with a retryable error parks and writes no AccountState (the fold is skipped), so 7 of 101 accounts have no state in this replay. The paid run showed 101 because the pilot had already computed a state for every account.
ACCOUNT-LEVEL STATE. The AccountState is per account but the CRM has 11.6 deals per account (max 15), so one state folds claims from every deal; its stage/owner winner is the latest across deals.

GROUND-TRUTH CAVEATS. OpportunityContactRole.Role, Opportunity.Type and NextStep are empty, so there is no role, motion or next-step truth. The CRM stage 'Closed' has no won/lost. The snapshot has no real stage history; the in-force stage is the loader's DERIVED stage events. The CRMArena emails were generated from CRM fields, so agreement with the CRM mostly shows the dataset repeating itself.
